near_miss.lead: *h2eyk- + *peku: ON eiga/eignir + fé ~ Ved. īśiṣe paśūnām 'you rule over the cattle'
near_miss.why_not: The ON anchors only coordinate the nouns (eignir eða lausa fé 'estates or movables'); in the other ON pivots eiga takes sakir/skuld, not fé, so no ON anchor has the verb + object pairing. collocates_8c --pair gives 237/3093 Germanic fé units with eiga, mostly the everyday 'átti fé' ('owned money'). Germanic eiga means plain possession, while Vedic īś- means lordship over livestock. The match is generic and the contexts are not congruent.

near_miss.lead: kin-slaying list: ON drepr föður sinn eða móður, bróður eða dóttur eða systur (óbótamaðr) ~ AVP mātṛhā pitṛhā svasṛhā (duṣkṛtaḥ)
near_miss.why_not: The concept is congruent (killers of kin as the worst offenders), but the verbs are not cognate (drepa vs han-), and the only shared material is kin terms, which any such list must contain. The ON text is a 13th-c. royal law code. No figure is carried by cognate material beyond the kin terms.

near_miss.lead: father/mother/brother enumeration (ON faðir eða móðir eða bróðir; Skt mātā pitā bhrātā; OIr athair/ingen, bráthair, mac/máthair)
near_miss.why_not: This is a generic enumeration of kin, with nothing beyond the kin terms themselves. The contexts differ: ON law on who may give a woman in marriage, an OIr list of legal pairs, Skt didactic verse.

near_miss.lead: head + feet (+ hide) of a slaughtered beast: ON hǫfuð ok fœtr ok húð ~ AVŚ śīrṣṇaḥ ... padā
near_miss.why_not: The ON is a practical rule on leaving the carcass remains behind; the AVŚ is a riddle hymn about cows and the cosmos. The context and syntax are not shared, and head/foot co-occur everywhere.

near_miss.lead: witness merism ON séð eða heyrt 'seen or heard'
near_miss.why_not: The Latin partner has only auris, and there is no cross-branch witness formula in the slab. Seen-or-heard is a universal legal merism.

near_miss.lead: ON legal pair líf eða limir 'life or limbs'
near_miss.why_not: This is a Germanic-internal alliterative pair; the Skt partner (ripu/mitra) shares nothing relevant.

near_miss.lead: kin bereft of kin in a catastrophe: MIr siur cen bráthair ... cen máthair cen athair ~ Arm. oč ordi hawr ... kʻoyr ełbawr
near_miss.why_not: Both are generic rhetoric of disaster built from kin terms. The MIr text is a learned Alexander translation, the Armenian a Christian history. No cognate verb or figure is shared.
The link is a false mapping (OIr línaid < *pleh1-, not *leyH-). There is no shared context.

near_miss.lead: ON bera orð föður síns ~ Lat. pater ... uerba det
near_miss.why_not: The meanings are unrelated (testimony vs 'deceive'); the shared words are only father + word.

near_miss.lead: season sequence (ON um várit ... um sumarit; Ved. vasanta, grīṣma ...)
near_miss.why_not: The ON is a narrative itinerary, the Vedic a ritual list of seasons; the season names are generic.

near_miss.why_not: The material shares no wording beyond basic kin terms and verbs.

error.correct_reading: ro lín = pret. 3sg of línaid 'fills' (< *pleh1-, cf. lán)
error.evidence: The object is na fántu / na glenntu ('filled the slopes/glens'); the same 'ro lín' recurs in mga:G303000:#1:1667, where the young man fills the horns.

error.correct_reading: lín 'net' (loan from Lat. līnum) or 'number'; not *leyH- 'pour'
error.evidence: In 'l lín fri h-íascach' (50 nets for fishing) the noun means 'nets'.
'in lín bíte i seasam' = 'the number that are standing'.

error.correct_reading: mann, acc. sg. of maðr ('gíftingar man[n]' = the marriage guardian)
error.evidence: The phrase is 'at leita þess við giftingar man'; the next clause, 'En gíftíngar maðr er...', gives the nominative of the same word.
ON stefna is a legal term of summoning, derived within Germanic from stef/stafr.

error.correct_reading: ben cen chéli; siur cen bráthair; cen máthair cen athair; Alaxandir
error.evidence: The OCR misreads b>h, n>ll and garbles the name; the parallel 'cen ... cen' series makes the intended text clear.

note: Second reading of 30 flagged bundles. No claims: every lead rests on kin terms or generic vocabulary, or on mapping errors. The best lead, ON eiga/fé ~ Ved. īśe paśūnām, was tested with collocates_8c; no ON anchor shows the verb + object pairing, so it is recorded as a near-miss.
